mainTopic: Relying on the majority, watching a שחיטה, and the rule that most people who slaughter are experts
overview: The amud opens by finishing an argument about רובא, following the majority. Even רבי מאיר must rely on the majority for פסח and קדשים, so the rule becomes: where you can check, you check; where you can't, you follow the majority. That same rule weakens the earlier proof for the רבנן. Next, רב נחמן quotes רב: you may eat from someone's שחיטה only if you watched it from beginning to end. The גמרא explains that רב means a known untrained שוחט who cut one סימן properly in front of us, because one good cut might just be luck. Then רב דימי בר יוסף asks why an agent's שחיטה is presumed done but his separating of תרומה is not. רב נחמן answers that if a stranger did the job, a שחיטה is still fine because most slaughterers are experts. A stranger's תרומה, however, is invalid without the owner's consent. Finally, the גמרא asks whether that rule is debated by תנאים. רב נחמן בר יצחק says everyone accepts it, and the dispute is really about a trash heap in the house. This leads to an apparent contradiction in רבי's statement, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What about the פסח and קדשים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר: how can anyone eat פסח and קדשים, if we never rely on the majority?
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסח offering and קדשים: what is there to say about them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority. It asks how, by his approach, anyone could eat the פסח or קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These animals must be eaten, but they cannot be fully checked for every possible defect before eating. So even רבי מאיר must rely on the majority of animals being healthy. The question is designed to force him to admit some reliance on רובא.

keyTerms.meaning: The Pesach offering, which must be eaten
Sacrificial meat, which has its own rules for eating
What is there to say? A question showing there is no good answer

phrases.english: The Pesach offering and sacrificial meat
phrases.notes: These come up because they have to be eaten, even though they can't be checked fully beforehand.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (before this section) about whether רבי מאיר ever relies on the majority.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's position that we worry about the minority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: פסח and קדשים must be eaten without full checking, so some reliance on the majority is unavoidable.

steps.title: Where checking is possible, check; where not, rely on the majority
steps.stepSummary: The forced answer for רבי מאיר: he relies on the majority only when checking is impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you must say: where it is possible to check, you check. Where it is not possible, it is not possible, and you follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the only possible answer for רבי מאיר. You check whenever you can, and you rely on the majority only when checking cannot be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why רבי מאיר still allows eating פסח and קדשים. He follows the majority when checking is impossible, but not when checking is possible. This sets up a two-part rule that the גמרא will reuse in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Where it is possible to check
Where it is not possible to check
Rather; introduces the answer you are forced to give

phrases.english: Rather, where it is possible, it is possible,
phrases.notes: He means: when you can check, you must check, and you don't rely on the majority.

phrases.english: where it is not possible, it is not possible.
phrases.notes: When you can't check, you have no choice, so you follow the majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases where checking is possible and cases where it is not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר never relies on the majority at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר relies on the majority only when checking is impossible.

steps.title: The same distinction weakens the proof for the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the same two-part rule to the רבנן, so the sources brought earlier no longer prove that we rely on the majority even when we could check.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: perhaps where it is possible to check, you check, and where it is not possible, you follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the distinction from Step 2 against the earlier proof. Maybe the רבנן also rely on the majority only when checking cannot be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier sources tried to show that we may rely on the majority right from the start, even when checking is possible. But all those sources might be cases where checking was impossible. So they prove nothing about cases where you could check.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too; the same reasoning applies to this case
The majority; following what is usually true

steps.whatToRemember: The rule "where you can check, check; where you can't, follow the majority" works for רבי מאיר. It also takes away the proof that the רבנן rely on the majority even when checking is possible.

phrases.english: Here too,
where it is possible, it is possible,
where it is not possible, it is not possible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the distinction from Step 2 and uses it to reject the earlier proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that one may rely on the majority from the start even when checking is possible
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sources may all be cases where checking was impossible, so they cannot prove the broader claim.

steps.title: Watching a שחיטה from beginning to end
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רב: you may eat from someone's שחיטה only if you watched him from start to finish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: if someone saw a person slaughter, and he saw him from beginning to end, he may eat from his slaughter. If not, he may not eat from it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. רב rules that seeing the whole שחיטה, from start to finish, is what permits you to eat the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Watching the whole process lets you confirm the שחיטה was done correctly. If you missed part of it, you may not eat. The גמרא will now ask exactly what kind of שוחט this rule is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: Kosher slaughter
From beginning to end
Permitted
Forbidden

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rav said:
If one saw someone who slaughtered,
if he saw him from beginning to end,
he is permitted to eat from his slaughter,
and if not, he is forbidden to eat from his slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, after the רובא discussion ended in Step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You may eat from a שחיטה only if you watched it from beginning to end.

steps.title: What case is רב talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case רב means. If the שוחט is known to be trained, watching is not needed. If he is known to be untrained, the rule is obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he knows the שוחט is trained, why do I need him to have seen it? And if he knows the שוחט is not trained, that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to pin down what kind of שוחט רב is talking about. It rules out the first two options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A known expert can be trusted without being watched, so רב's rule would be unnecessary for him. For a known non-expert, of course you must watch, so רב would be teaching nothing new. This sets up the third option in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? A request to define the situation
Trained; knows the laws of שחיטה
Obvious! Meaning this would not need to be said
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If he knows that he is trained,
why do I need that he saw?
And if he knows that he is not trained,
it is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case behind רב's statement in Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב means a trained שוחט, an untrained one, or one whose training is unknown.

steps.title: If his training is unknown, we should rely on the majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries the third case, where his training is unknown, and challenges it: most people who do שחיטה are experts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case where he does not know whether the שוחט is trained or not. But then let us say: most people who handle שחיטה are experts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last option, where nobody knows if this שוחט is trained. It immediately challenges that case too, because we could simply rely on the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since most people who do שחיטה are experts, an unknown שוחט should be trusted without being watched. So רב's demand to watch from beginning to end seems unnecessary in this case as well. This ties back to the רובא discussion from Steps 1 to 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Most people who are involved in שחיטה
Experts
Let us say; suggests a reasoning that would undo the case

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the conclusion. The גמרא is raising a challenge to רב, and step 8 answers it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It connects back to the question of whether we rely on the majority when checking, here by watching, is possible.

phrases.english: Rather, where he does not know
whether he is trained or not trained,
let us say: most of those involved in slaughter
are experts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא, דְּלָא יְדַע אִי גְּמִיר אִי לָא גְּמִיר, לֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries the third case left open by Step 5 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's requirement to watch the שחיטה from beginning to end
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Most people who do שחיטה are experts, so an unknown שוחט should be trusted without being watched.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows we trust that most שוחטים are experts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where a chicken found slaughtered is presumed kosher. It learns from this that most people who do שחיטה are experts, so the same should apply in רב's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it taught: if someone found a slaughtered chicken in the market, or told his agent 'go slaughter' and later found it slaughtered, it is presumed properly slaughtered. So we say most people who do שחיטה are experts. Here too, let us say most people who do שחיטה are experts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge from step 6 with a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows we trust a slaughter even when we don't know who did it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא nobody watched the slaughter and the שוחט is unknown, yet the chicken is allowed. That only makes sense if we rely on the majority: most שוחטים are experts. So in רב's case of a שוחט whose training is unknown, we should also rely on the majority and not demand watching.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption: what we assume to be true unless shown otherwise
An agent sent to do something on someone's behalf

keyTerms.term: רוֹב מְצוּיִין אֵצֶל שְׁחִיטָה מוּמְחִין הֵן
keyTerms.meaning: Most people who do שחיטה are experts in it
Apparently / this shows that

phrases.english: Isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Where one found a slaughtered chicken in the marketplace,
or where he said to his agent, 'Go out, slaughter,'
and he went and found it slaughtered —
its presumed status is that it was properly slaughtered.
Apparently we say:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹב מְצוּיִין אֵצֶל שְׁחִיטָה מוּמְחִין הֵן.
phrases.english: Most of those who are involved with slaughter are experts.
Here too, let us say:
phrases.notes: Here means רב's case, where we don't know whether the שוחט is trained.

phrases.aramaic: רוֹב מְצוּיִין אֵצֶל שְׁחִיטָה מוּמְחִין הֵן!
phrases.english: Most of those involved with slaughter are experts!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge raised in step 6
steps.raayaObject: That we rely on the majority of שוחטים being experts even without watching
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about a chicken found slaughtered in the market or by a שליח
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule (step 4), read as applying to a שוחט whose training is unknown
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the majority lets us eat when nobody saw the slaughter at all, it should let us eat when the שוחט's training is merely unknown

steps.title: רב means an untrained שוחט who did one סימן right
steps.stepSummary: רב's case is a שוחט known to be untrained who cut one סימן properly in front of us. That one good cut doesn't prove the second was good, because the first may have been luck.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it's where we know he is not trained, and he slaughtered one סימן properly in front of us. You might think: since this one was good, that one was also good. רב teaches us: this one just happened to work out for him. The other one, maybe he paused or maybe he pressed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by going back to the case of a known untrained שוחט and adding a detail. That detail makes רב's rule no longer obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the untrained case seemed obvious. Now we add that he did one סימן properly while we watched, so you might think he did the second one right too. רב teaches that one good cut by an untrained person could be chance, so you must watch the whole שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually: the גמרא keeps a case it had seemed to reject
One of the two pipes that must be cut in שחיטה (windpipe and food pipe)
You might have thought... so it teaches us: shows why a rule had to be said
It just happened by chance
Pausing in the middle of cutting, which makes the שחיטה invalid
Pressing the knife down instead of drawing it, which makes the שחיטה invalid

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a case of unknown training. The שוחט is known to be untrained, so the majority of experts doesn't help. The only question is whether one good סימן proves the second.

phrases.english: Actually, it is where he knows that he is not trained,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְגוֹן דִּשְׁחַט קַמַּן חַד סִימָן שַׁפִּיר.
phrases.english: and where he slaughtered one סימן properly in front of us.
You might have said:
since this one was done properly, that one was also done properly,
so it teaches us:
this one just happened to work out for him,
the other one — perhaps he paused, perhaps he pressed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 6–7 by going back to the known-untrained case from step 5, and adds a detail (one good סימן) that answers step 5's objection that the case would be obvious
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) with an added detail
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One properly cut סימן shows he can do it, so the second was surely fine too
steps.terutzMaskana: One good cut by an untrained person may be chance; you must watch the whole שחיטה
steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule (watch from start to finish) is about a known untrained שוחט. Even one good סימן in front of you doesn't vouch for the other.

steps.title: Is a slaughter by your agent presumed done properly?
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי בר יוסף asks רב נחמן: if you send your agent to slaughter and later find the animal slaughtered, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי בר יוסף asked רב נחמן: one who says to his agent 'go out and slaughter,' and then goes and finds it slaughtered, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. It is about whether we may assume the agent did the slaughter that was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner didn't see who slaughtered the animal, so he doesn't know for sure that his agent did it properly. רב דימי wants to know whether we presume it was slaughtered properly.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him / raised a question before him
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב דִּימִי בַּר יוֹסֵף מֵרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Dimi bar Yosef asked Rav Nachman:
One who says to his agent, 'Go out and slaughter,'
and he went and found it slaughtered, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בעא מיניה רב דימי בר יוסף מרב נחמן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related question about presumptions involving a שליח, echoing the second case of the ברייתא in step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an animal found slaughtered after sending a שליח is presumed properly slaughtered

steps.title: Yes, it is presumed properly slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the animal is presumed properly slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: its presumed status is that it was properly slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רב דימי's first question. The animal is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the ברייתא from step 7. We may assume the slaughter was done properly even though the owner didn't see it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is presumed to be properly slaughtered

phrases.english: He said to him: its presumed status is that it was properly slaughtered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animal is presumed properly slaughtered

steps.title: Is תרומה your agent was sent to separate presumed separated?
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי asks a parallel question. If you send your agent to separate תרומה and find it separated, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: One who says to his agent 'go out and separate תרומה,' and he goes and finds it separated, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי asks the same kind of question again, now about separating תרומה instead of שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The setup is exactly the same as the שחיטה case: the owner sent an agent, and later finds the job done. The question is whether the presumption that worked for שחיטה also works for תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce that must be separated and given to a כהן
Already separated (תרומה has been taken from it)

phrases.english: One who says to his agent, 'Go out and separate תרומה,'
and he went and found that תרומה was separated, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel question to step 9, switching from שחיטה to תרומה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether produce found with תרומה separated after sending a שליח is presumed properly separated

steps.title: No, it is not presumed separated
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that here there is no presumption that the תרומה was separated, unlike the שחיטה case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: its presumed status is not that תרומה was separated.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the opposite answer for תרומה. We may not assume the job was done properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases look the same, but רב נחמן treats them differently: שחיטה is presumed done, תרומה is not. This sets up רב דימי's challenge in step 13, and רב נחמן explains the difference in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no presumption that תרומה was separated

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the שליח cases are all treated the same. The setup is identical, but רב נחמן rules differently for תרומה than for שחיטה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The different answers for two cases that look alike show that a שליח's job is not always presumed done. This difference is what the next part of the sugya needs to explain.

phrases.english: He said to him: its presumed status is not that תרומה was separated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11, giving the opposite result from step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no presumption that the תרומה was separated

steps.title: רב דימי's either-way challenge
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי argues that רב נחמן's two answers contradict each other. If an agent is presumed to do his job, it should work for תרומה too. If he is not, it should not work for שחיטה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if we presume an agent does his mission, then תרומה should also count. And if we don't presume that, then שחיטה shouldn't count either.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי challenges רב נחמן's two answers from Steps 10 and 12, which seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases look the same on the surface: an agent was sent, and later the job is found done. רב דימי assumes the only possible reason to trust the result is a presumption that agents do their jobs. That reason should cover both cases or neither.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you look at it. Introduces an argument that fails under either option.
A legal presumption
An agent carries out his mission

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it,
if there is a presumption that an agent carries out his mission,
then even תרומה too should count,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אֵין חֲזָקָה שָׁלִיחַ עוֹשֶׂה שְׁלִיחוּתוֹ –
phrases.english: and if there is no presumption that an agent carries out his mission,
then even slaughter should not count either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the contrast between רב נחמן's answers in Steps 10 and 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's different rulings for שחיטה and תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both rulings depend on one presumption about agents, so they must come out the same.

steps.title: The difference is who else might have done it
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says there is no presumption that agents do their jobs. If a stranger did the שחיטה, it is still valid, because most people who slaughter are experts. If a stranger separated תרומה, it is invalid, because it was done without the owner's consent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Think it over for a long time and you'll see. Really, there is no presumption that an agent does his mission. With שחיטה, even if maybe someone else heard and went and slaughtered, most people involved with slaughter are experts. With תרומה, maybe someone else heard and went and separated it. Then he separated without the owner's consent, and תרומה separated without the owner's consent is not תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רב דימי. He moves the difference away from the agent and onto the possibility that some stranger did the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן agrees there is no presumption about agents. So he must consider that someone else did it. For שחיטה, a stranger is fine, since most slaughterers are experts. For תרומה, a stranger's act is useless because only the owner or his chosen agent can separate.

keyTerms.meaning: A כור of salt. A huge amount, meaning: think about it for a long time.
Really, actually. Introduces the true position.

keyTerms.term: רוֹב מְצוּיִין אֵצֶל שְׁחִיטָה מוּמְחִין הֵן
keyTerms.meaning: Most people involved with slaughter are experts
One who separates תרומה without the owner's knowledge or consent

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule רוב מצויין אצל שחיטה מומחין הן, which the rest of this section examines.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying the agent is trusted for שחיטה. He says the meat is fine even if someone else slaughtered it.

phrases.english: He said to him:
After you eat a kor of salt over it,
phrases.notes: A כור is a huge measure. He means that if you think it over long enough, you'll get it.

phrases.english: really, there is no presumption
that an agent carries out his mission,
and as for slaughter,
even if perhaps another person
heard, and went and slaughtered,
most of those involved with slaughter
are experts.
As for תרומה,
perhaps another person
heard, and went and separated it,
so he is one who separates without consent,
and one who separates without consent,
his תרומה is not תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב דימי's either-way challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases on a new basis: the validity of an act done by a stranger
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings depend on whether agents are presumed to do their jobs.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no such presumption. שחיטה works anyway because most slaughterers are experts. תרומה fails because a stranger's separation lacks the owner's consent.

steps.title: Is the 'most slaughterers are experts' rule debated by תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders whether רוב מצויין אצל שחיטה מומחין הן is a dispute between תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא: someone lost goats and roosters and found them slaughtered. רבי יהודה forbids them and רבי חנינא בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי permits them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that 'most people involved with slaughter are experts' is a dispute of תנאים? As it was taught: if someone's goats and roosters got lost, and he went and found them slaughtered, רבי יהודה forbids them and רבי חנינא, son of רבי יוסי הגלילי, permits them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and brings a ברייתא as its source. It is setting up the suggestion that comes in Step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no agent was sent at all. The only way to permit the animals is to assume whoever slaughtered them was an expert. So the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי חנינא might be about exactly that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it is a dispute of תנאים? A suggestion that a rule is debated by earlier sages.
His young goats
Forbids
Permits

phrases.english: Shall we say

phrases.aramaic: רוֹב מְצוּיִין אֵצֶל שְׁחִיטָה מוּמְחִין הֵן
phrases.english: that 'most of those involved with slaughter are experts'
is a dispute of תנאים?
As it was taught:
One whose young goats and roosters were lost,
and he went and found them slaughtered:
Rabbi Yehuda forbids them,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי מַתִּיר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, permits them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא: רוֹב מְצוּיִין אֵצֶל שְׁחִיטָה מוּמְחִין הֵן תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the rule רב נחמן used in Step 14 and asks whether it is debated
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rule 'most slaughterers are experts' is accepted by everyone or is debated by תנאים

steps.title: רבי splits the case by where the animals were found
steps.stepSummary: Within the ברייתא, רבי says רבי יהודה's view makes sense when the animals were found in a trash heap. רבי חנינא's view makes sense when they were found in a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: רבי יהודה's words seem right when he found them in a trash heap, and the words of רבי חנינא, son of רבי יוסי הגלילי, seem right when he found them in a house.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues: רבי offers a middle position that applies each opinion to a different place where the animals were found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the location changes the picture. Animals thrown in the trash look like they were discarded, perhaps because the שחיטה was bad. Animals found in a house look like someone meant to eat them.

keyTerms.meaning: The words seem correct
A trash heap

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
The words of Rabbi Yehuda seem correct
where he found them in a trash heap,

phrases.aramaic: וְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
phrases.english: and the words of Rabbi Chanina, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, seem correct
where he found them in a house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דְּבָרִים שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in Step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals found slaughtered in a trash heap are forbidden. Animals found slaughtered in a house are permitted.

steps.title: Suggesting the dispute is about 'most slaughterers are experts'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יהודה and רבי חנינא argue about exactly this rule. One holds that most slaughterers are experts and the other does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? One master holds we say most people involved with slaughter are experts, and the other master holds we don't say that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the suggestion it began in Step 15. It proposes that the ברייתא's argument is about the rule רב נחמן relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this reading is right, רבי חנינא, who permits, accepts the rule. רבי יהודה, who forbids, rejects it. Then רב נחמן's answer in Step 14 would hold only according to one side of a dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not so? Introduces a proposed reading.
They disagree
One master holds... and the other master holds

steps.whatToRemember: The rule רוב מצויין אצל שחיטה מומחין הן explains why שחיטה by an unknown person can be valid. The גמרא is now checking whether everyone agrees to it.

phrases.english: Is it not about this that they disagree,
that one master holds:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִינַן רוֹב מְצוּיִין אֵצֶל שְׁחִיטָה מוּמְחִין הֵן,
phrases.english: we say that most of those involved with slaughter are experts,
and the other master holds:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן רוֹב מְצוּיִין אֵצֶל שְׁחִיטָה מוּמְחִין הֵן?
phrases.english: we do not say that most of those involved with slaughter are experts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the suggestion begun in Step 15 by reading the ברייתא's dispute
steps.raayaObject: That רוב מצויין אצל שחיטה מומחין הן is a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about lost goats and roosters found slaughtered

steps.title: Everyone agrees most slaughterers are experts; the real dispute is the trash heap in the house
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the idea that the תנאים argue about רוב מצויין אצל שחיטה מומחין הן. Everyone accepts that rule. They argue only about whether a person tends to throw a נבילה onto a trash heap inside his house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: No. Everyone agrees that most people who slaughter are experts. If the animals were found in a house, everyone agrees they are permitted. If they were found in a trash heap in the market, everyone agrees they are forbidden. They argue about a trash heap in the house. One Sage holds that a person does throw his נבילה onto a trash heap in the house. The other Sage holds that a person does not throw his נבילה onto a trash heap in the house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק pushes back on the suggestion from step 17. He says the two תנאים do not argue about whether slaughterers are experts at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides accept that most slaughterers are experts. So the only open question is where the animal was found. A house means it was slaughtered properly. A market trash heap means it was a discarded נבילה. The argument is only about the in-between case, a trash heap inside the house. רבי יהודה forbids it because people do toss a נבילה there. רבי חנינא permits it because people do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone; all opinions agree
A trash heap in the marketplace
A trash heap inside the house
Tends to throw; is likely to toss
An animal that died without a valid שחיטה, forbidden to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה rejects רוב מצויין אצל שחיטה מומחין הן here. According to רב נחמן בר יצחק, he fully accepts it. His only question is whether the animal was ever slaughtered, or was a נבילה someone threw away.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the rule that most slaughterers are experts from being a dispute between תנאים. That rule is what רב נחמן relied on back in step 14.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לָא,
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: No,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא רוֹב מְצוּיִין אֵצֶל שְׁחִיטָה מוּמְחִין הֵן,
phrases.english: everyone agrees that most of those who deal with slaughter are experts,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְבַיִת – דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי,
phrases.english: and in a house, everyone agrees that it is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: בְּאַשְׁפָּה שֶׁבַּשּׁוּק – דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּאָסוּר,
phrases.english: in a trash heap in the market, everyone agrees that it is forbidden,
where they argue is a trash heap in the house:
phrases.notes: He means a trash heap that belongs to the house, as opposed to a public one in the market.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר אָדָם עָשׂוּי לְהַטִּיל נִבְלָתוֹ בְּאַשְׁפָּה שֶׁבַּבַּיִת,
phrases.english: one Sage holds a person tends to throw his נבילה onto a trash heap in the house,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה, who forbids the animals.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר אֵין אָדָם עָשׂוּי לְהַטִּיל נִבְלָתוֹ בְּאַשְׁפָּה שֶׁבַּבַּיִת.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds a person does not tend to throw his נבילה onto a trash heap in the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 17 that the תנאים argue about whether most slaughterers are experts.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי יהודה and רבי חנינא argue about רוב מצויין אצל שחיטה מומחין הן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be explained differently. It is about where people throw a נבילה, not about whether slaughterers are experts.

steps.title: What does 'trash heap' mean in רבי's first statement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading against רבי's comment. רבי sided with רבי יהודה for a 'trash heap'. That cannot mean the market trash heap, which everyone forbids. So it must mean the trash heap in the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said that רבי said: רבי יהודה's view makes sense when he found them in a trash heap. Which trash heap? If you say the market trash heap, you just said everyone agrees it is forbidden there! So it must obviously mean the trash heap in the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts checking רבי's statement against the new explanation. This is a setup: it pins down the first half of רבי's words before looking at the second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב נחמן בר יצחק, a market trash heap is forbidden by everyone. So רבי would have no reason to single out רבי יהודה there. That forces 'trash heap' to mean the trash heap in the house. In that case, רבי agrees with רבי יהודה to forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: What? Which one is meant?
If you say; suppose it means
Rather, is it not so that
It is obvious

phrases.english: The Master said: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting back רבי's line from the ברייתא in step 16.

phrases.aramaic: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁמְּצָאָן בְּאַשְׁפָּה.
phrases.english: The words of Rabbi Yehuda appear correct when he found them in a trash heap.
What trash heap? If you say a trash heap in the market,

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמְרַתְּ דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּאָסוּר!
phrases.english: but you said everyone agrees that it is forbidden!
Rather, is it not obvious that it means a trash heap in the house?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר, אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁמְּצָאָן בְּאַשְׁפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב נחמן בר יצחק's framework from step 18 to the first half of רבי's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which trash heap רבי means when he sides with רבי יהודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It must be the trash heap in the house, because everyone forbids the market trash heap.

steps.title: 'House' must also mean the trash heap in the house, so רבי contradicts himself
steps.stepSummary: Under the same framework, רבי's 'house' cannot mean an actual house, which everyone permits. So it must also mean the trash heap in the house. Now רבי both forbids and permits the same case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the end of רבי's statement: and the words of רבי חנינא son of רבי יוסי הגלילי make sense when he found them in a house. Which house? If you say an actual house, you just said everyone agrees it is permitted there! So it must obviously mean the trash heap in the house. Then רבי contradicts רבי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the second half of רבי's statement the same way. It finds that both halves are about the same case, which creates a contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב נחמן בר יצחק, an actual house is permitted by everyone. So 'house' must mean the trash heap in the house. In the first half, רבי forbade that case with רבי יהודה. In the second half, he permits it with רבי חנינא. The same רבי cannot hold both, so רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter part of a statement or teaching
Actual; literally
A contradiction between one statement of רבי and another statement of רבי

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not with רבי יהודה or רבי חנינא. It is that רבי himself ends up siding with both of them about the exact same case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This contradiction threatens רב נחמן בר יצחק's whole reading of the dispute. The גמרא will need to resolve it.

phrases.english: Say the latter part:

phrases.aramaic: וְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
phrases.english: and the words of Rabbi Ḥanina, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, appear correct
when he found them in a house.
What house? If you say an actual house,

phrases.aramaic: הָאָמְרַתְּ דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי!
phrases.english: but you said everyone agrees that it is permitted!
Rather, it obviously means a trash heap in the house.
It is difficult: Rabbi contradicts Rabbi!
phrases.notes: In the first half רבי forbade the trash heap in the house. Here he permits that same case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the analysis begun in step 19 by reading the second half of רבי's statement, and finds that it clashes with the first half.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation in step 18 that the dispute is only about the trash heap in the house.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that explanation, both 'trash heap' and 'house' in רבי's words must mean the trash heap in the house. That makes רבי forbid and permit the same case.
